report.source_text: A lumbar puncture was performed, the results of which revealed a 0.5 mL colourless sample of fluid with an isolated elevated protein level of 1.77 g/L (0.15–0.45). Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) glucose was 3.9 mmol/L, white cell count <0.001 ×109/L and red blood cell <0.001 ×109/L. In addition, microbiology and culture of the CSF sample yielded no growth of organisms. Oligoclonal band studies illustrated a pattern consistent with a passive transfer of oligoclonal IgG from a systemic inflammatory response and was not indicative of intrathecal synthesis (typically seen in conditions such as multiple sclerosis).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old British Caucasian man with no prior medical history presented to accident and emergency approximately 2 weeks following ChAdOx1 COVID-19 vaccination with acute onset of back pain, distal paraesthesia in hands and feet, and symmetrical progressive ascending muscle weakness. Physical examination revealed reduced motor strength in all four limbs, decreased light touch sensation and proprioception in lower limbs from groin distally, bilateral areflexia in lower limbs, and ataxic gait. Lumbar puncture demonstrated markedly elevated CSF protein (1.77 g/L) with minimal pleocytosis (<0.001 ×10⁹/L WBC and RBC) and normal glucose (3.9 mmol/L), consistent with GBS albuminocytologic dissociation. Oligoclonal bands showed passive transfer pattern from systemic inflammation, not intrathecal synthesis. Nerve conduction study performed early in disease course showed patchy attenuation of upper limb motor responses. MRI spine demonstrated globally thickened cauda equina nerve rootlets bilaterally (particularly at S1) with prominent ventral nerve root enhancement and pial enhancement of conus medullaris, consistent with autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy. MRI head was normal. The patient was admitted for FVC monitoring and commenced on intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg daily for 5 days. On day 3 of treatment, FVC deteriorated to 2.6 L, prompting pre-emptive admission to intensive care for mechanical ventilation monitoring. The patient successfully completed the IVIG course without requiring mechanical ventilation. Neurological symptoms showed slow recovery, and the patient remained under observation in a quaternary neurology centre receiving ongoing specialist neurology and physiotherapy input.

final.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old British Caucasian man with no prior medical history presented to accident and emergency approximately 2 weeks following ChAdOx1 COVID-19 vaccination with acute onset of back pain, distal paraesthesia in hands and feet, and symmetrical progressive ascending muscle weakness. Physical examination revealed reduced motor strength in all four limbs, decreased light touch sensation and proprioception in lower limbs from groin distally, bilateral areflexia in lower limbs, and ataxic gait. Lumbar puncture demonstrated markedly elevated CSF protein (1.77 g/L) with minimal pleocytosis (<0.001 ×10⁹/L WBC and RBC) and normal glucose (3.9 mmol/L), consistent with GBS albuminocytologic dissociation. Oligoclonal bands showed passive transfer pattern from systemic inflammation, not intrathecal synthesis. Nerve conduction study performed early in disease course showed patchy attenuation of upper limb motor responses. MRI spine demonstrated globally thickened cauda equina nerve rootlets bilaterally (particularly at S1) with prominent ventral nerve root enhancement and pial enhancement of conus medullaris, consistent with autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy. MRI head was normal. The patient was admitted for FVC monitoring and commenced on intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg daily for 5 days. On day 3 of treatment, FVC deteriorated to 2.6 L, prompting pre-emptive admission to intensive care for mechanical ventilation monitoring. The patient successfully completed the IVIG course without requiring mechanical ventilation. Neurological symptoms showed slow recovery, and the patient remained under observation in a quaternary neurology centre receiving ongoing specialist neurology and physiotherapy input.
